subject: School Committee Structural and Election Reform
overview: The subcommittee met to review the current organization and legal duties of the School Committee and discuss potential charter revisions. Members prioritized improving public participation, evaluating the mayor's role as chair, and exploring staggered terms or ward-based representation.

items.title: School Committee Roles and Responsibilities
items.summary: The chair provided an overview of the School Committee’s current seven-member structure, two-year terms, and core responsibilities including budgeting, policy-making, and superintendent oversight.

items.title: Public Participation Concerns
items.summary: Members discussed concerns regarding the committee's accessibility to citizens and the current rules requiring pre-submission of public comments to the superintendent.

items.title: Subcommittee Member Expectations
items.summary: Subcommittee members identified key areas for the charter review, including the mayor's role as chair, strengthening city council partnerships, and increasing parent involvement.

items.title: School Facilities Map Review
items.summary: The subcommittee reviewed a map of school facilities, noting that school locations are clustered and do not align evenly with current city wards.

items.title: Stakeholder Outreach Planning
items.summary: The group planned to survey former and current school committee members via email and proposed hosting an in-person forum in January to brainstorm structural reforms.

items.title: Statewide Peer Input
items.summary: The committee decided to solicit feedback from the Massachusetts Association of School Committees (MASC) regarding other districts' experiences with ward representation and staggered terms.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: A member of the public and former school committee member noted appreciation for the subcommittee's points but declined to offer a formal statement.
